rationale: The literature presents conflicting evidence regarding the neuroimaging hallmark of anterior temporal pole white matter hyperintensities (WMH) in NOTCH3 cysteine-sparing variants. On one hand, Luo et al. (2026) demonstrated that two siblings with a homozygous cysteine-sparing missense variant in EGFr19 (c.3373G>A, p.Glu1125Lys) showed confluent temporal pole WMH (Fazekas grade 3) alongside elevated cerebral microbleed (CMB) density (2.15 vs. 0.4 counts/cm³). On the other hand, comprehensive systematic review data from Cao et al. (2024) evaluating 298 individuals with cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 mutations found that while CMB frequencies are significantly elevated (72.73%) compared to classic CADASIL, anterior temporal pole and external capsule WMH are characteristically rare or absent. Similarly, Kim et al. (2006) showed that cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants (such as p.Arg75P) show significantly less frequent involvement of the anterior temporal pole compared to classic cysteine-altering CADASIL mutations.

evidence.text: Two siblings harboring a homozygous cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 missense variant in EGFr19 (c.3373G>A, p.Glu1125Lys) presented with confluent periventricular and temporal pole white matter hyperintensities (Fazekas grade 3) and a significantly higher cerebral microbleed density than controls.

source.quote: MRI showed confluent periventricular and temporal pole white matter hyperintensities (Fazekas grade 3) and numerous deep CMBs, particularly in the basal ganglia and cerebellum. Quantitatively, total CMB density was higher compared with controls (mean 2.15 counts/cm³ vs. 0.4 ± 0.2 counts/cm³; p = 0.008).

evidence.text: In a systematic review of 298 individuals with NOTCH3 cysteine-sparing variants, cerebral microbleeds were significantly more frequent than in classic CADASIL, but anterior temporal pole and external capsule hyperintensities were rarely observed.

source.title: Phenotypes associated with NOTCH3 cysteine-sparing mutations in patients with clinical suspicion of CADASIL: a systematic review
source.quote: Compared with CADASIL patients, cognitive impairment and cerebral microbleed frequencies were significantly higher in patients with NOTCH3 cysteine-sparing mutations, while the white matter hyperintensities in anterior temporal polar and external capsule were rarely observed.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in NOTCH3 cause an autosomal recessive pediatric leukodystrophy characterized by severe spastic tetraparesis and periventricular white matter lesions without anterior temporal pole involvement.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: Emerging evidence shows that biallelic loss-of-function variants, unlike the gain-of-function variants underlying CADASIL, define a distinct autosomal recessive leukodystrophy characterized by early-onset pyramidal signs, epilepsy, and white matter abnormalities, thereby expanding the phenotypic and molecular spectrum of NOTCH3-related disorders.

conflicts: Luo et al. (2026) report that homozygous cysteine-sparing variants in EGFr19 present with confluent Fazekas 3 temporal pole white matter hyperintensities, whereas systematic review and cohort data (Cao et al., 2024; Kim et al., 2006) demonstrate that cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants typically exhibit rare or significantly reduced anterior temporal pole hyperintensities compared to classic CADASIL.

new_directions.question_text: Do homozygous cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants located specifically in distal EGFr domains (e.g., EGFr19) produce a different radiological pattern of temporal pole involvement compared to proximal cysteine-sparing variants (e.g., exon 3/EGFr1-2)?
new_directions.rationale: Most described cysteine-sparing mutations cluster in exon 3 and lack temporal pole lesions, whereas the EGFr19 homozygous variant demonstrated marked temporal pole involvement, suggesting possible domain-specific radiological divergence.
